summary: Charles Otto Blagden (1864–1949) was a scholar of linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at Dulwich College and Corpus Christi College, Oxford (~1882–1886), and later held a post at SOAS University of London (~1917–1935).

Charles Philip Brown (1798–1884) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Haileybury/East India Company College (~1814–1817) and under traditional teachers Kodandarama Panthulu, Venkatasivasastri Tippabhatla, and Advaitabrahmasastri Vatthyam. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1817–1854) and was Professor of Telugu at the University of London (~1865–1879).

Charles Ramble (born 1957) specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Durham University (~1975–1978) and under Michael Aris (~1980–1985). His career includes posts at Tribhuvan University, Wolfson College, Oxford (~2000–2010), the University of Oxford (2002–2005), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (from 2009).

Charles Rieu (1820–1902) was an Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at the University of Geneva and the University of Bonn (1840–1843) under Christian Lassen, Jean Humbert, Georg Freytag, and Johann Gildemeister. He served at the British Museum from 1847 and as Adams Professor of Arabic at the University of Cambridge.

Charles Rockwell Lanman (1850–1941) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Yale, Berlin, Tübingen, and Leipzig under William Dwight Whitney, James Hadley, Theodore Dwight Woolsey, James Dwight Dana, Rudolf von Roth, Albrecht Weber, Georg Curtius, and August Leskien. He taught at Johns Hopkins University (1876–1880) and Harvard University (1880–1926).

Charles S. Prebish (born 1944) works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Case Western Reserve University and under David M. Miller and Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as Professor of Religious Studies at Pennsylvania State University (~1972–2007) and held posts at the University of Toronto and University of Calgary.

Charles Taliaferro (born 1952) is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Goddard College, Harvard Divinity School, the University of Rhode Island, and Brown University, and served as a professor at St. Olaf College (~1985–2022).

Charles Taylor (born 1931) is a philosopher who studied at Selwyn House School, McGill University (~1948–1952), and Balliol College, Oxford (~1952–1955). He held faculty posts at McGill University (~1961–1998), the University of Montreal (~1967–1971), and Northwestern University (~2002–2008).

Charles Wei-hsun Fu (1933–1996) specialized in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He completed his studies at National Taiwan University (~1952–1960) and the University of Illinois System (~1965–1969), and held an academic post at Ohio University (~1969–1972).

Charles Wilkins (1749–1836) was an Indologist who studied under Kalinatha (~1778–1784). He co-founded The Asiatic Society in 1784 and served as librarian for the East India Company (from 1770 and 1801), librarian at the India Office Library (1800), and examiner at East India Company College (1805).

Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin (1832–1899) was a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He earned a doctorate in law at the University of Liège (-1855) and served as director of Collège Saint-Quirin (~1861) before becoming a professor at KU Leuven / Université catholique de Louvain from 1871 to 1899.

Charlotte Furth (1934–2022) was a scholar in Sinology and history and archaeology. She held professorial posts at California State University (~1969–1989) and the University of Southern California (~1989–2008).

Chatral Sangye Dorje (1913–2015) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied under numerous traditional masters, including Sera Khandro Dewé Dorje, Dorje Dradul, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, and later succeeded Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje.

Chatsumarn Kabilsingh (born 1944) specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied at Visva-Bharati University, McMaster University, and Magadh University, and taught in the Department of Philosophy and Religion at Thammasat University (~1973–2000).

Chen-kuo Lin (born 1950) works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Temple University (graduated 1991) and served as Professor and Distinguished Professor at National Chengchi University (attested 1997–1999, 2014–2018), with visiting posts at Leiden University and IIAS.
Cheng Yen (born 1937) is a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied as a disciple under Yinshun in 1963. She founded the Tzu Chi Foundation in 1966 and Tzu Chi University in 2000.
Cheryl A. Crowley is a scholar in Japanology. She completed her studies under William R. LaFleur, Philip B. Yampolsky, Ryuichi Abe, and Barbara Ruch.

Cheung Tsui Lan Liza works in Buddhist studies. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013), studying under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti and teacher Toshiichi Endo.
Chhime Rigdzing (1922–2002) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and held a post at Visva-Bharati University.

Chi Chen Ho is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She studied under Hsuan Hua and doctoral supervisor Robert E. Buswell Jr., earning a PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles (-2010), where she also served as a Teaching Assistant.
